<style>
    @font-face {
        font-family: 'Niradei';
        src: url('/assets/klik_pos/fonts/Niradei-Regular.woff2') format('woff2');
        font-weight: normal;
        font-style: normal;
    }
    @font-face {
        font-family: 'Niradei';
        src: url('/assets/klik_pos/fonts/Niradei-SemiBold.woff2') format('woff2');
        font-weight: 600;
        font-style: normal;
    }
    @font-face {
        font-family: 'Niradei';
        src: url('/assets/klik_pos/fonts/Niradei-Bold.woff2') format('woff2');
        font-weight: bold;
        font-style: normal;
    }
    @font-face {
        font-family: 'Khmer OS Muol Light';
        src: url('/assets/klik_pos/fonts/KhmerOSmuollight.ttf') format('truetype');
        font-weight: normal;
        font-style: normal;
    }
    @font-face {
        font-family: 'Khmer OS Battambang';
        src: url('/assets/klik_pos/fonts/KhmerOSbattambang.ttf') format('truetype');
        font-weight: normal;
        font-style: normal;
    }

    /* Defensive reset - this template is rendered inside Frappe's .print-format-gutter >
       .print-format wrapper (print.bundle.css, which imports bootstrap), for all three
       consumers: the browser printview, the POS preview panel, and frappe.get_print(as_pdf=True)
       used for the Telegram image. Never rely on inherited sizing/spacing from that wrapper. */
    .print-format-gutter, .print-format {
        margin: 0 !important;
        padding: 0 !important;
        background: none !important;
        box-shadow: none !important;
    }

    /* Real @page rule - honored by actual browsers (the printview "Print" button, and the
       cashier's own Ctrl+P). Chrome and Firefox both respect this at print time. */
    @page {
        size: 148mm 210mm;
        margin: 0;
    }

    /* Frappe's PDF pipeline (both wkhtmltopdf and its own "chrome" pdf_generator) does NOT read
       the @page rule above - frappe/utils/pdf.py's read_options_from_html() / browser.py's
       _parse_pdf_options_from_html() instead scrape a handful of non-standard properties off a
       CSS rule whose selector is *exactly* ".print-format", and browser.py hardcodes a 15mm
       left/right margin fallback whenever page-width/page-height aren't found this way. Real
       browsers simply ignore these bogus property names on a real selector, so this rule is safe
       to ship - it does nothing outside Frappe's own PDF generation.

       page-size: A5 is required too, not just cosmetic - without it, frappe/utils/pdf.py's
       _set_default_page_size() injects "page-size: A4" (from Print Settings) alongside our
       page-width/page-height. wkhtmltopdf's *output page* still comes out physically correct
       (explicit width/height win there), but it lays out the HTML content itself against A4's
       wider internal viewport reference and then squeezes that onto the declared A5 page,
       uniformly shrinking every element - this was the actual cause of rows rendering far
       shorter than their declared height. ("page-size: Custom" looks like the "proper" fix per
       that function's own branching, but Frappe's Custom branch never clears the "page-size" key
       it already scraped from this CSS, so the literal string "Custom" reaches wkhtmltopdf's CLI
       and crashes it - "A5" is both a valid CLI value and physically identical to our explicit
       width/height, so it sidesteps that bug entirely.) */
    .print-format {
        page-size: A5;
        page-width: 148mm;
        page-height: 210mm;
        margin-top: 0mm;
        margin-bottom: 0mm;
        margin-left: 0mm;
        margin-right: 0mm;
    }

    .a5-invoice-root, .a5-invoice-root * {
        box-sizing: border-box;
    }
    .a5-invoice-root {
        font-family: 'Khmer OS Battambang', 'Niradei', Arial, sans-serif;
        font-size: 10px;
        line-height: 1.4;
        color: #000;
    }

    /* One .a5-page per 14-item chunk. Deliberately not named "page-break" - Frappe's own
       printview.html looks for exactly that class name and force-styles it. */
    .a5-page {
        position: relative;
        width: 148mm;
        height: 210mm;
        /* Deliberately no overflow:hidden. paginate_invoice_items only ESTIMATES how many
           description lines an item needs in order to decide how many items fit per page - it
           never truncates the description text itself, since a description (e.g. a custom
           roofing-sheet cutting spec) must never be silently cut off. If that estimate is ever
           slightly low, the safe failure mode is a description visibly spilling past where the
           next section was expected to start - not a hidden clip that quietly drops content the
           workshop needed to prepare from. */
        background: #fff;
    }
    .a5-page.a5-page-brk {
        page-break-after: always;
        break-after: page;
    }

    /* --- Header: absolute-positioned blocks, no flex/grid (wkhtmltopdf silently collapses
       both to plain block boxes - this template must render correctly under either
       pdf_generator) --- */
    .header-left {
        position: absolute;
        top: 8mm;
        left: 8mm;
        width: 35mm;
    }
    .header-center {
        position: absolute;
        top: 10mm;
        left: 45mm;
        width: 60mm;
        text-align: center;
    }
    .qr-center-right {
        position: absolute;
        top: 8mm;
        left: 69mm;
        width: 60mm;
        text-align: center;
        z-index: 1;
    }
    .header-right {
        position: absolute;
        top: 8mm;
        left: 107mm;
        width: 33mm;
    }

    .header-left img, .header-right img {
        width: 100%;
        height: auto;
        max-height: 25mm;
        object-fit: cover;
        display: block;
        margin-bottom: 4px;
    }

    .contact-info {
        text-align: center;
        margin-top: 4px;
    }
    .contact-icons {
        text-align: center;
        margin-bottom: 2px;
    }
    .contact-icons img {
        display: inline-block;
        width: 18px;
        height: 18px;
        margin: 0 2px;
        vertical-align: middle;
    }
    .phone-numbers {
        color: #d91a1a;
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 14px;
        line-height: 1.2;
    }

    .invoice-badge {
        border: 1.5px solid #0f9c2e;
        border-radius: 5px;
        display: inline-block;
        padding: 8px 15px 6px;
        color: #0f9c2e;
        margin-bottom: 6px;
        border-bottom: 4px solid #0f9c2e;
        border-left: 4px solid #0f9c2e;
    }
    .invoice-title-km {
        font-size: 14px;
        font-family: 'Khmer OS Muol Light', sans-serif;
        line-height: 1.6;
    }
    .invoice-title-en {
        font-size: 15px;
        font-weight: 600;
        line-height: 1.1;
    }
    /* CHANGED 1.6 -> 1.4 to match the mockup. This is what makes the whole header block sit
       ~3mm higher; the header ends at ~42.6mm from the top of the page, which is what buys the
       clearance for the subheader at 47mm. If Khmer subscripts visually clip here, raise it to
       1.5 max and drop the .subheader top to 48mm. */
    .business-details {
        color: #1313a8;
        font-family: 'Niradei', sans-serif;
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 14px;
        line-height: 1.4;
    }

    .checkbox-group {
        color: #0f9c2e;
        font-family: 'Arial', sans-serif;
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 9.5px;
        text-align: left;
        margin-top: 8px;
    }
    .checkbox-item {
        margin-bottom: 3px;
    }
    /* An actual checkbox glyph (U+2610 / U+2611) rather than a CSS-drawn square, so there is no
       border anywhere in this block. Needs a font that carries those codepoints - DejaVu Sans
       is the reliable one on a Debian/Ubuntu bench and is listed first. If these come out as
       tofu boxes in the PDF, the server is missing it: `apt install fonts-dejavu-core`, then
       restart the bench so wkhtmltopdf rescans the font cache. */
    .checkbox-box {
        display: inline-block;
        vertical-align: bottom;
        width: 20px;
        font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Noto Sans Symbols 2', 'Segoe UI Symbol', Arial, sans-serif;
        font-size: 20px;
        line-height: 1;
        text-align: left;
        margin-right: -4px;
    }
    .checkbox-item span.label {
        vertical-align: middle;
        border:none;
        font-size: 10px;
    }

    /* --- Subheader --- */
    /* Two rows of one table, both flush left at 8mm: the customer line, then date (left) /
       N deg (right). Since the customer line is no longer indented it has to clear the
       .header-left phone-number block, which bottoms out around 49mm - hence top: 50mm.
       Both rows are now 13px/1.4 (~4.8mm each) plus a 0.5mm gap, so the block ends at
       ~60.1mm and the table starts at 61.5mm. */
    .subheader {
        font-family: 'Arial', sans-serif;
        position: absolute;
        top: 50mm;
        left: 8mm;
        width: 132mm;
        color: #1313a8;
    }
    .subheader table {
        width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse;
    }
    /* !important is load-bearing: print.bundle.css ships ".print-format td, .print-format th
       { padding: 10px !important }", which otherwise wins over a plain "padding: 0" here
       regardless of selector specificity and silently adds ~5mm to this row. */
    .subheader td {
        border: none !important;
        padding: 0 !important;
        font-size: 13px;
        font-weight: bold;
        line-height: 1.4;
        vertical-align: bottom;
    }
    .subheader td.invoice-no {
        text-align: right;
        white-space: nowrap;
    }
    #sale-invoice-no{
        color:red !important;
    }
    /* Deliberately carries no font or colour of its own - it is a <td> inside the same table as
       the date, so it picks up .subheader td's 13px / bold / 1.4 / #1313a8 verbatim. The only
       job left here is the gap to the date line and clipping an over-long customer name. */
    .subheader td.customer-row {
        padding-bottom: 0.5mm !important;
        white-space: nowrap;
        overflow: hidden;
    }

    /* --- Main table --- */
    /* 61.5mm - the customer line moved from 10px to 13px to match the date, which added ~1.4mm
       to the subheader. Header 9mm + 14 rows at 6.5mm + 3 footer rows at 7mm = 121mm, so the
       table bottom lands at 182.5mm on a 210mm page. */
    .table-container {
        position: absolute;
        top: 61.5mm;
        left: 8mm;
        width: 132mm;
    }

    /* border: none matches the mockup, where an inline style="border: none" overrides the
       stylesheet's 1.5px. With border-collapse the outer edge then shows the cells' own 1px, so
       the whole grid is a uniform hairline. Put back "border: 1.5px solid #1313a8" here if you
       prefer the heavier outer frame. */
    table.items {
        width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse;
        border: none;
        table-layout: fixed;
    }
    /* Root cause of the row-height overhead chased across earlier iterations: Frappe's own
       print.bundle.css ships ".print-format td, .print-format th { padding: 10px !important; }"
       (twice, in fact - 6px then 10px). Since our print format's markup lives inside that exact
       ".print-format" wrapper for every rendering path (browser printview, POS preview,
       frappe.get_print PDF), that !important beats any non-!important padding rule here
       regardless of selector specificity - it was adding ~5.3mm of unwanted vertical padding to
       every cell, not a font-metrics or box-sizing quirk as first suspected. Row height still
       lives on a plain block-level div INSIDE each cell (.td-box/.th-box) rather than on the
       <td>/<th> itself as further defense-in-depth - a div's `height` is a hard, reliably
       respected box dimension in every engine, whereas a table cell's own `height` is only ever
       a minimum the layout engine can pad out further. */
    table.items th, table.items td {
        border: 1px solid #1313a8 !important;
        padding: 0 4px !important;
    }
    table.items th {
        color: #0f9c2e;
        font-weight: bold;
        text-align: center;
        font-size: 11px;
    }
    .th-box {
        height: 9mm;
        line-height: 13px;
        padding-top: 1.1mm;
    }
    .col-no { width: 6%; text-align: center; color: #1313a8; font-weight: bold; font-size: 11px; }
    .col-name { width: 38%; }
    .col-qty { width: 14%; text-align: center; }
    .col-price { width: 18%; text-align: right; }
    .col-amount { width: 24%; text-align: right; }

    /* 14px is the DEFAULT item-row size, not always the rendered one: an item name too wide for
       .col-name gets an inline "font-size: Npx" (14 down to 8, per row) from
       paginate_invoice_items - see fit_item_name_font_size in utils.py, which measures the real
       name against this cell's width using the same vendored font declared above. Plain (non-
       !important) font-size here on purpose - that is what lets the inline style win. The
       overflow/ellipsis below therefore only ever fires for a name that still does not fit at
       8px. Row height stays 6.5mm at every size, so the slot math is unaffected; line-height is
       the vertical-centering trick (== box height), which keeps a shrunken name centred too. If
       you change this size, or .col-name's 38%, update the geometry constants in utils.py. */
    .td-box {
        height: 6.5mm;
        line-height: 6.5mm;
        overflow: hidden;
        white-space: nowrap;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
        font-size:14px;
    }

    /* "table.items td.foo-cell" (not just ".foo-cell") deliberately - these need to out-specify
       the "table.items th, table.items td" padding reset above, not just match its !important. */
    table.items td.footer-notes-cell {
        border-left: none !important;
        border-bottom: none !important;
        border-right: none !important;
        padding: 6px !important;
        vertical-align: top;
    }
    table.items td.footer-label-cell {
        border: none !important;
        text-align: right;
        color: #0f9c2e;
        font-weight: bold;
        vertical-align: middle;
        padding: 0 8px 0 0 !important;
        font-size: 10.8px;
        height: 7mm;
    }
    table.items td.footer-value-cell {
        border: 1px solid #1313a8 !important;
        font-size:14px;
        font-weight:600;
        text-align: right;
        padding: 0 6px !important;
    }

    /* Full-width spec line for the handful of items that carry a description (e.g. a roofing
       sheet's custom cutting order) - a niche, per-item case, not shown for ordinary items.
       Deliberately no height/overflow constraint - see paginate_invoice_items and the .a5-page
       comment above: this text must never be cut off, only the page-planning estimate is
       approximate. line-height is an explicit px value, not a unitless multiplier, for the same
       Khmer-font-metric reason as the rest of this table. */
    table.items td.description-cell {
        border-top: none !important;
        text-align: left;
        /* !important because of the same Bootstrap print reset the COLOUR HARDENING block below
           exists for - it targets `*` directly, so a plain (non-!important) colour here would
           lose to it and print as pure black instead of this dark grey. */
        color: #333 !important;
        /* Same font-size as the item name (.td-box) above it, per request. line-height is a
           normal ~1.25x reading ratio, not copied from .td-box's "line-height == box height"
           vertical-centering trick - this cell wraps to multiple lines, so that trick would leave
           huge gaps between them. Khmer needs that full ratio: stacked vowel signs/subscript
           consonants take real vertical space above and below the baseline, so keep line-height
           at ~1.25x whenever this font-size changes, or adjacent spec lines collide.
           estimate_description_slots' chars_per_line in utils.py is calibrated to this same
           font-size - change the two together. */
        font-size: 14px;
        line-height: 18px;
        /* Left indent is 3x the other cells' 4mm - deliberately visually offset from the item
           name above it, not aligned with it. */
        padding: 1mm 4mm 1mm 12mm !important;
        white-space: normal;
    }

    /* The mockup puts "បញ្ជាក់ៈ" beside the two note lines via display:flex. flex is not usable
       here (wkhtmltopdf collapses it to a plain block), so this is the inline-block equivalent.
       The two spans must stay adjacent in the markup with NO whitespace between them, or the
       collapsed space widens the gap. */
    .footer-notes {
        color: #d91a1a;
        font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 11px;
        line-height: 1.3;
    }
    .footer-notes .fn-label {
        display: inline-block;
        vertical-align: top;
        white-space: nowrap;
        margin-right: 4px;
    }
    .footer-notes .fn-text {
        display: inline-block;
        vertical-align: top;
    }

    /* Was a nested <table> - which is a descendant of table.items and therefore inherited the
       "table.items td { border: 1px solid #1313a8 !important }" rule above, drawing visible
       boxes around both signature captions. Two inline-blocks avoid the nested-table trap
       entirely. Again: no whitespace between the two divs in the markup. */
    .footer-signatures {
        margin-top: 15px;
        color: #1313a8;
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 11px;
        text-align: center;
    }
    .footer-signatures .sig {
        display: inline-block;
        vertical-align: top;
        width: 49.5%;
        text-align: center;
    }

    .continuation-notice {
        text-align: center;
        color: #1313a8;
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 10px;
        padding: 6px;
    }

    /* ------------------------------------------------------------------
       COLOUR HARDENING - this is why everything was coming out black.

       Frappe's print.bundle.css imports Bootstrap, whose print stylesheet ships
       `@media print { * { color: #000 !important; background: transparent !important; } }`.
       That fires for the browser's Print dialog, for wkhtmltopdf, and for Frappe's chrome
       pdf_generator - i.e. everywhere except the on-screen preview, which is exactly why the
       preview looked right and the printed output didn't.

       Two consequences drive the shape of every rule below:

       1. It carries !important, so our plain `color:` declarations lost outright. A class
          selector out-specifies `*` (0,1,0 vs 0,0,0), so restating each colour with
          !important reliably wins it back.
       2. It targets `*` DIRECTLY on every element, not just the containers. Inheritance never
          gets a chance - setting a colour on .business-details does nothing for the three
          <div>s inside it, because those divs are matched by `*` themselves. Hence the
          `X, X *` reach on each rule.

       Kept in one block at the end of the stylesheet rather than scattered through the rules
       above, so the intent stays legible and the whole thing is one deletion if a future
       Frappe version drops the Bootstrap print reset. */

    .a5-invoice-root {
        -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
        print-color-adjust: exact;
    }
    /* Bootstrap's reset also forces `background: transparent`, which matters for the
       frappe.get_print(as_pdf=True) -> Telegram image path: a transparent page can flatten to
       black in the PNG conversion rather than to white paper. */
    .a5-page {
        background: #fff !important;
        -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
        print-color-adjust: exact;
    }

    /* Red - phone numbers and the terms note */
    .phone-numbers, .phone-numbers *,
    .footer-notes, .footer-notes * {
        color: #d91a1a !important;
    }

    /* Green - INVOICE badge, status labels, column headers, footer labels */
    .invoice-badge, .invoice-badge *,
    .checkbox-group, .checkbox-group *,
    table.items th, table.items th *,
    table.items td.footer-label-cell {
        color: #0f9c2e !important;
    }
    .invoice-badge {
        border-color: #0f9c2e !important;
    }

    /* Blue - business details, subheader, row numbers, signatures, continuation notice */
    .business-details, .business-details *,
    .subheader, .subheader *,
    table.items th.col-no, table.items th.col-no *,
    table.items td.col-no, table.items td.col-no *,
    .footer-signatures, .footer-signatures *,
    .continuation-notice, .continuation-notice * {
        color: #1313a8 !important;
    }
    /* th.col-no is listed above deliberately: in the mockup `.col-no` (0,1,0) out-specifies the
       bare `th` colour rule (0,0,1), so the "ល.រ / No" header renders blue there, not green.
       Move it out of this block and into the green one if you'd rather it match the other four
       headers. */
</style>

<div class="a5-invoice-root">
{% set pages = paginate_invoice_items(doc.items, pos_profile=doc.pos_profile) %}
{# Gross-up ratio so Unit Price / Amount print tax-INCLUSIVE, whether tax is configured
   inclusive or exclusive. For On-Net-Total taxes this is exact; equals 1 (no change) when
   there is no tax. #}
{% set incl_ratio = (doc.grand_total / doc.net_total) if doc.net_total else 1 %}
{% set customer_phone = doc.contact_mobile or frappe.db.get_value("Customer", doc.customer, "mobile_no") %}
{% set is_delivered = doc.custom_delivery_status == "Delivered" %}
{% set is_pickup = doc.custom_delivery_status == "Self Pickup" %}
{% for page in pages %}
<div class="a5-page{{ '' if page.is_last else ' a5-page-brk' }}">

    <div class="header-left">
        <img src="/assets/klik_pos/images/invoice_khmer/left.jpg" alt="Steel Products">
        <div class="contact-info">
            <div class="contact-icons">
                <img src="/assets/klik_pos/images/invoice_khmer/phone.png" alt="Phone">
                <img src="/assets/klik_pos/images/invoice_khmer/telegram.png" alt="Telegram">
            </div>
            <div class="phone-numbers">
                092 95 34 24<br>
                071 9 554 654
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <div class="header-center">
        <div class="invoice-badge">
            <div class="invoice-title-km">វិក្កយបត្រ</div>
            <div class="invoice-title-en">INVOICE</div>
        </div>
        <div class="business-details">
            <div>មានលក់ដែកទីបមូល ជ្រុង ស-ខ្មៅ</div>
            <div>ដែក V, U, I, H & តោន</div>
            <div>សង្ក័សីភ្លឺធំ តូច ទ ប្រអប់ គ្រប់ប្រភេទ</div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <div class="qr-center-right">
        {% set qr = get_invoice_qr_png(doc.name) %}
        {% if qr %}<img src="{{ qr }}" style="width: 70px; height: auto;">{% endif %}
    </div>

    <div class="header-right">
        <img src="/assets/klik_pos/images/invoice_khmer/right.jpg" alt="Roofing Products">
        <div class="checkbox-group">
            <div class="checkbox-item">
                <span class="checkbox-box">☐</span><span class="label">បានកាត់.................</span>
            </div>
            <div class="checkbox-item">
                <span class="checkbox-box">{{ "☑" if is_delivered else "☐" }}</span><span class="label">បានដឹក...................</span>
            </div>
            <div class="checkbox-item">
                <span class="checkbox-box">{{ "☑" if is_pickup else "☐" }}</span><span class="label">បានមកយក............</span>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <div class="subheader">
        <table>
            <tr>
                <td colspan="2" class="customer-row">អតិថិជន: {{ doc.customer_name }}{% if customer_phone %} / {{ customer_phone }}{% endif %}</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td>ថ្ងៃទី {{ frappe.utils.formatdate(doc.posting_date, "dd") }} ខែ {{ frappe.utils.formatdate(doc.posting_date, "mm") }} ឆ្នាំ{{ frappe.utils.formatdate(doc.posting_date, "yyyy") }}</td>
                <td class="invoice-no">N° <span id="sale-invoice-no">{{ doc.name }}</span></td>
            </tr>
        </table>
    </div>

    <div class="table-container">
        <table class="items">
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th class="col-no"><div class="th-box"><div>ល.រ</div><div>No</div></div></th>
                    <th class="col-name"><div class="th-box"><div>មុខទំនិញ</div><div>Name of Goods</div></div></th>
                    <th class="col-qty"><div class="th-box"><div>ចំនួន</div><div>Quantity</div></div></th>
                    <th class="col-price"><div class="th-box"><div>តម្លៃរាយ</div><div>Unit Price</div></div></th>
                    <th class="col-amount"><div class="th-box"><div>តម្លៃសរុប</div><div>Amount</div></div></th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                {% for row in page.rows %}
                <tr class="item-row">
                    <td class="col-no"><div class="td-box">{{ row.no }}</div></td>
                    {% if row.item %}
                    <td class="col-name"><div class="td-box"{% if row.name_font_size %} style="font-size: {{ row.name_font_size }}px"{% endif %}>{{ row.item.item_name }}</div></td>
                    <td class="col-qty"><div class="td-box">{{ row.item.qty|int if row.item.qty == row.item.qty|int else row.item.qty }}</div></td>
                    <td class="col-price"><div class="td-box">{{ frappe.utils.fmt_money(row.item.net_rate * incl_ratio, currency=doc.currency) }}</div></td>
                    <td class="col-amount"><div class="td-box">{{ frappe.utils.fmt_money(row.item.net_amount * incl_ratio, currency=doc.currency) }}</div></td>
                    {% else %}
                    <td class="col-name"><div class="td-box"> </div></td>
                    <td class="col-qty"><div class="td-box"> </div></td>
                    <td class="col-price"><div class="td-box"> </div></td>
                    <td class="col-amount"><div class="td-box"> </div></td>
                    {% endif %}
                </tr>
                {% if row.description %}
                <tr class="desc-row">
                    <td colspan="5" class="description-cell">{{ row.description }}</td>
                </tr>
                {% endif %}
                {% endfor %}

                {% if page.is_last %}
                <tr>
                    <td colspan="3" rowspan="{{ 4 if doc.total_taxes_and_charges else 3 }}" class="footer-notes-cell">
                        <div class="footer-notes"><span class="fn-label">បញ្ជាក់ៈ</span><span class="fn-text">ដែកទិញហើយមិនអាចដូរយកវិញបានទេ<br>ឥវ៉ាន់មិនទាន់ទូទាត់ជាកម្មសិទ្ធិរបស់ដេប៉ូ</span></div>
                        <div class="footer-signatures"><div class="sig">អ្នកទិញ / The Buyer</div><div class="sig">អ្នកលក់ / The Seller</div></div>
                    </td>
                    <td class="footer-label-cell">សរុប / Total</td>
                    <td class="footer-value-cell">{{ frappe.utils.fmt_money(doc.grand_total, currency=doc.currency) }}</td>
                </tr>
                {% if doc.total_taxes_and_charges %}
                <tr>
                    <td class="footer-label-cell">ពន្ធ (រួមក្នុងតម្លៃ) / Tax (incl.)</td>
                    <td class="footer-value-cell">{{ frappe.utils.fmt_money(doc.total_taxes_and_charges, currency=doc.currency) }}</td>
                </tr>
                {% endif %}
                <tr>
                    <td class="footer-label-cell">កក់មុន / Deposit</td>
                    <td class="footer-value-cell">{{ frappe.utils.fmt_money(doc.paid_amount, currency=doc.currency) }}</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td class="footer-label-cell">នៅខ្វះ / Balance</td>
                    <td class="footer-value-cell">{{ frappe.utils.fmt_money(doc.outstanding_amount, currency=doc.currency) }}</td>
                </tr>
                {% else %}
                <tr>
                    <td colspan="5" class="continuation-notice">ទំព័រ {{ page.page_no }}/{{ page.total_pages }} - សូមមើលទំព័របន្ទាប់ / continued on next page</td>
                </tr>
                {% endif %}
            </tbody>
        </table>
    </div>

</div>
{% endfor %}
</div>
